subject: Re: Raptor Science - DPA redlines & SCCs execution timeline
messages:
From: Megan Hayes <megan@raptorsci.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@raptorsci.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines and SCCs — timeline

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call earlier. We pulled together a short list of follow-ups from our legal team: they want to confirm (1) whether Redwood will accept the EU SCCs without an export carveout, (2) the processing role mapping for our subcontractors, and (3) a reasonable timeline to get an executed DPA in place before our pilot starts on 2026-12-01. Attached is Raptor's proposed DPA v3 with their in‑line comments.

Can you confirm: do you have capacity for a 2x review cycle this week? If you think any of the SCCs language will require an escalation to your privacy/legal partners, please flag immediately.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Megan
Director of Legal Operations
Raptor Science

Attachments: Raptor_DPA_v3_redlines.docx

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Megan Hayes <megan@raptorsci.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and SCCs — timeline

Megan — thanks for sending. We reviewed the file briefly and can confirm Redwood's standard position on SCCs: we accept the EU SCCs as the baseline; we do not agree to a broad export carveout that would bypass contractual safeguards.

Next steps from our side:
- Ben (legal) will run through the in‑line redlines and propose countertext on data export and subprocessor roles.
- Jordan (privacy ops) will produce a subprocessor mapping and the proposed delegation matrix by EOD Wednesday.
- I can commit to two review cycles this week; goal is to have an agreed DPA to DocuSign by Friday 2026-11-06 if there are no material escalations.

If your team needs a shorter cadence, we can do a 30-minute tranche call tomorrow at 11:00 PT.

— Irene
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Raptor DPA redlines — proposed responses

Irene/Jordan — draft notes after first pass on Megan's redlined DPA:

1) SCCs/export carveout: Raptor inserted a clause asking for an explicit carveout to allow transfers for regulatory reasons without prior notice. We should push back and offer the standard SCCs + a narrow mutual legal requirement exception that mirrors our MSA language.

2) Subprocessor roles: Raptor's table asks Redwood to take processor role for monitoring services delivered by third parties in all territories. Suggest we clarify that Redwood acts as processor for model serving and hosting; subprocessors used for observability/monitoring are processors for performance management only and subject to same SCCs. Jordan — can you draft a short delegation matrix to attach?

3) Data residency/exports: If Raptor requires specific routing constraints for EU-origin data we can offer region pins in Dedicated or Private but not as a contractual carveout in hosted. Propose: add a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) option in Exhibit B for customers needing extra controls.

I'll prepare tracked changes and the cover memo. Attaching the initial redlines for review.

-Ben
Associate General Counsel (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Raptor_DPA_v3_redlines_response.docx

From: Contracts <contracts@raptorsci.com>
To: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Megan Hayes <megan@raptorsci.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and SCCs — quick questions before response

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifying items from our side before you send tracked changes: 
- The "mutual legal requirement" language sounds promising; can you share a one‑paragraph example of the text you intend to use? Our privacy counsel wants to ensure it's symmetrical.
- For the subprocessor mapping: is Jordan's delegation matrix going to list by category (e.g., monitoring, backups, analytics) or name specific vendors? They prefer categories first, names later.
- If Redwood proposes a TIA as an Exhibit B option, will that be an addendum we (Raptor) can sign and bind independently of the MSA, or is it only effective when hosted on Dedicated/Private?

We want to avoid scope-creep; the pilot must be able to begin on 2026-12-01 with basic processing safeguards in place. If an exec escalation is needed for carveouts, please flag immediately.

Regards,
Contracts Team
Raptor Science

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Contracts <contracts@raptorsci.com>, Megan Hayes <megan@raptorsci.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and SCCs — next steps and timeline

Team — quick status update and attachments.

Ben's tracked changes are attached (Raptor_DPA_v3_redlines_response.docx) and include: a concise mutual legal requirement paragraph, tightened subprocessor role language (categories + sample vendor list in an annex), and an optional Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) we can attach as Exhibit B. The TIA is drafted so Raptor can sign it with the MSA (preferable) or sign it later if you choose Dedicated/Private hosting.

Jordan's subprocessor/delegation matrix is in the checklist PDF and follows the category-first approach.

Proposed timeline:
- Friday 2026-11-06 EOB: Raptor reviews Ben's tracked changes and returns any final asks (one short cycle only).
- Monday 2026-11-09: finalize DPA + TIA; Redwood to issue DocuSign envelope.
- Target execution: Tuesday 2026-11-10 to keep pilot prep on track.

If Raptor needs exec backing, Ben, Jordan and I are aligned to escalate to Commercial/Legal leadership the same day.

Next action: Megan — can you confirm whether Raptor prefers the TIA signed with the MSA now or to keep it optional for Dedicated/Private? If we don't hear back by EOB Friday we'll proceed with the TIA attached to the DPA and include an execution note that hosting-specific controls apply when Dedicated/Private is selected.

Thanks — Irene
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Raptor_DPA_v3_redlines_response.docx, SCCs_Execution_Checklist.pdf
